title: Mean under a product distribution
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite type, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$. The product mean of $f$ is its expectation when the $n$ coordinates are sampled independently according to $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$f$ is a real-valued function on $n$-tuples from $\Omega$
